req.title: Password hashing uses generate_password_hash
req.statement: The system shall store passwords via werkzeug generate_password_hash rather than plaintext.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-035 requires that passwords are stored via werkzeug's generate_password_hash rather than plaintext. The violation was test[4] having kind=negative but heuristic=STC; negative tests must use heuristic=NEG. Fix: change test[4] heuristic from STC to NEG. All other tests are preserved exactly as they were. Tests cover: (1) positive/EP — registered user's stored password is a werkzeug hash not plaintext; (2) negative/NEG — wrong password yields 200 with error, correct yields 302; (3) boundary/BVA — single-char password is hashed; (4) positive/DT — hash format matches werkzeug structure and is salted; (5) negative/NEG — empty password registration is rejected or if accepted the stored value is still a hash not empty string.

tests.name: test_password_stored_as_hash_not_plaintext
actions: POST /auth/register with username='hashcheck' and password='secret123'
Query the database for the stored password of 'hashcheck'
Assert stored value is not equal to plaintext 'secret123'
Assert stored value starts with werkzeug hash prefix (pbkdf2, scrypt, or argon2)
Assert check_password_hash(stored, 'secret123') returns True
expected: Stored password starts with a known werkzeug hash method prefix
trace: R-FLASKR-035: passwords stored via generate_password_hash not plaintext
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db
from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'hashcheck', 'password': 'secret123'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = 'hashcheck'").fetchone()
    stored = row['password']

assert stored != 'secret123', 'Password must not be stored as plaintext'
assert stored is not None
assert len(stored) > 20, 'Hash must be longer than plaintext'
assert check_password_hash(stored, 'secret123') is True, 'Hash must verify with check_password_hash'
valid_prefixes = ('pbkdf2:', 'scrypt:', 'argon2')
assert any(stored.startswith(p) for p in valid_prefixes), f'Hash prefix not recognised: {stored[:20]}'
os.unlink(path)

Assert HTTP 200 (re-render login page with error)
Assert error message 'Incorrect password.' appears in response body
POST /auth/login with username='test' and password='test' (correct)
Assert HTTP 302 redirect to index

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r_wrong = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'WRONG'})
assert r_wrong.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r_wrong.status_code}'
assert b'Incorrect password.' in r_wrong.data, 'Expected Incorrect password. error'

r_correct = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r_correct.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r_correct.status_code}'
assert r_correct.headers['Location'] == '/'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = 'test'").fetchone()
    stored = row['password']
assert stored != 'test', 'Stored password must not equal plaintext'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_single_char_password_is_hashed_not_stored_plaintext
actions: POST /auth/register with username='bvauser' and password='x' (single character — minimum meaningful boundary)
Assert HTTP 302 redirect
Query database for stored password
Assert stored value != 'x'
Assert check_password_hash(stored, 'x') is True
Assert check_password_hash(stored, 'X') is False (case-sensitive boundary)
Assert len(stored) > 1 (hash is longer than single char)
expected: Stored password is a hash, not the single character 'x'
Hash verifies correctly for 'x' but not 'X'
trace: R-FLASKR-035: even minimum-length passwords must be hashed
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db
from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'bvauser', 'password': 'x'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = 'bvauser'").fetchone()
    stored = row['password']

assert stored != 'x', 'Single-char password must not be stored as plaintext'
assert len(stored) > 1, f'Hash length {len(stored)} must be > 1'
assert check_password_hash(stored, 'x') is True, 'Hash must verify for correct char'
assert check_password_hash(stored, 'X') is False, 'Hash must NOT verify for wrong case'
assert check_password_hash(stored, '') is False, 'Hash must NOT verify for empty string'

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'bvauser', 'password': 'x'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302, f'Login expected 302, got {r_login.status_code}'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_hash_format_uses_generate_password_hash_directly
actions: Call generate_password_hash('mypassword') directly to get reference hash format
Register user 'dtuser' with password 'mypassword' via POST /auth/register
Retrieve stored hash from database
Assert stored hash format matches werkzeug hash structure (contains ':' separator)
Assert stored hash is NOT equal to the reference hash (hashes are salted/unique)
Assert both hashes verify against 'mypassword' via check_password_hash
expected: Stored hash format is consistent with werkzeug generate_password_hash output
Two hashes of same password differ (salted)
trace: R-FLASKR-035: generate_password_hash is the specific function required
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db
from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash, generate_password_hash

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

reference_hash = generate_password_hash('mypassword')
assert check_password_hash(reference_hash, 'mypassword') is True

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'dtuser', 'password': 'mypassword'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = 'dtuser'").fetchone()
    stored = row['password']

assert stored != 'mypassword', 'Must not store plaintext'
assert stored != reference_hash, 'Salted hashes of same password must differ'
assert ':' in stored, 'Werkzeug hash must contain colon separator'
assert check_password_hash(stored, 'mypassword') is True, 'Stored hash must verify'
assert check_password_hash(reference_hash, 'mypassword') is True, 'Reference hash must verify'
assert check_password_hash(stored, 'wrongpassword') is False, 'Must not verify wrong password'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_wrong_username_login_returns_error
preconditions: Fresh database with pre-loaded fixture: user 'test' exists
actions: POST /auth/login with username='nonexistent' and password='test'
Assert HTTP 200 (re-render login page with error)
Assert error message 'Incorrect username.' appears in response body
Confirm no session is established for nonexistent user
expected: HTTP 200 with 'Incorrect username.' in body for unknown username
trace: R-FLASKR-035: hash verification only runs for known users; unknown username must be rejected before hash check

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'nonexistent', 'password': 'test'})
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r.status_code}'
assert b'Incorrect username.' in r.data, f'Expected Incorrect username. in response, got: {r.data[:200]}'

with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess, 'No user_id should be in session for failed login'

os.unlink(path)
